newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up as secondaries buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up as secondaries buoyant.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended higher on Thursday, boosted by buying of secondliners despite a sell-off in some blue-chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 2.84 points, or 0.43 percent, to close at 662.24 points after touching a low of 658.11 points midway through the afternoon session.
Advancers led decliners by 66 to 55 with 59 issues unchanged.
Brokers said trading was dominated by investors who targeted second-liners including newly-listed companies such as Surya Semesta, Daya Sakti Unggul and Mitra Rajasa.

Brokers said investors, led by locals, were also snapping up secondaries such as property firm Modern Land and hotel operator Sahid Jaya mostly on speculation of possible link up with foreign firms or merger talks.

Modern Land has denied the rumours, saying it had no plans that have not already been announced. It closed 650 rupiah higher at 3,300 rupiah on 31.5 million shares after scaling to an intra-day high of 3,875 rupiah.
Newly-listed property firm Surya Semesta was the most active stock on a volume of about 55.4 million shares. It ended at 1,000 rupiah against an offer price of 975 rupiah.
Transportation firm Mitra Rajasa closed 125 rupiah higher at 2,150 rupiah on active trading on talks of a possible expansion to air transportation and city buses.
Telkom was up 25 rupiah to 3,675 rupiah after further government confirmation on Thursday it had no intention of abolishing Telkom's monopoly ahead of schedule.

In contrast to active buying in secondaries, some investors continued selling off blue-chips counters such as cigarette firm Sampoerna, cement maker Semen Gresik and telecommunications service provider Indosat but their volumes were modest.
Brokers ascribed it to profit-taking ahead of the long weekend. The exchange will be closed on Friday for Good Friday and Monday for the fiscal year end and reopens on April 1.
Total turnover on Thursday was relatively big at 671.5 billion rupiah with about 306.2 million shares changing hands.
